paragraphs.heading: No gaps between values
paragraphs.text: A quantity that is measured with numbers can be either continuous or discrete. It is continuous over a stretch if, whenever it can take two real values, it can also take every value between them. So a variable that can land anywhere in some range of the real numbers is continuous there. Statistics treats continuous and discrete variables as separate data types, each described by its own kind of probability distribution.

paragraphs.heading: The discrete opposite
paragraphs.text: A variable is discrete around a value if there is a real gap on each side of that value that the variable can never land in. Put another way, every allowed value sits some positive distance from its nearest allowed neighbour. The allowed values are either finitely many or countably infinite. Typical examples are variables that must be whole numbers, or that can only be 0 or 1.

paragraphs.heading: Calculus and density
paragraphs.text: Methods of calculus are often used on problems with continuous variables, for instance in continuous optimization problems. Those methods do not fit discrete variables easily, which instead appear in problems such as integer programming. In statistical theory, the chances for a continuous variable can be written using a probability density function, while a discrete variable uses a probability mass function.

paragraphs.heading: Time, smooth or in steps
paragraphs.text: How time is treated changes the mathematics. If time is continuous, the rule for how something changes over time is a differential equation. A related idea is the instantaneous rate of change: how much one quantity changes compared with another at a single moment. If time moves in separate steps, the rule is instead called a difference equation.

paragraphs.heading: Mixing both kinds
paragraphs.text: A single variable can be discrete over part of the number line and continuous over another part. A mixed random variable has a probability distribution with both a discrete piece and a continuous piece. Waiting in a queue is an example: the chance of waiting exactly zero time is a discrete piece, while any nonzero wait is measured on a continuous time scale. In physics, especially quantum mechanics, Dirac delta functions are often used to handle both pieces in one framework.

paragraphs.heading: Switches and mixed models
paragraphs.text: In regression analysis, some variables are allowed only the values 0 and 1. Such a dummy variable works like a switch, turning a part of an equation on or off, and it can mark which subgroup of a study each person belongs to. A model with several variables can mix discrete and continuous ones. For example, a study of the risk of psychological disorders might pair one yes-or-no measure of psychiatric symptoms with one continuous measure of cognitive performance.
